subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond the existing `messages.suppressToolErrors` boolean, and what safety semantics should it use for failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config and user-visible failure delivery: it can improve hosted chat UX, but it can also hide failed mutations that the current policy intentionally surfaces.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after regression coverage proves failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep the boolean path
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and narrow this request to docs or channel-specific leak bugs.

options.title: Split narrow leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and handle remaining Feishu, exec-like, lifecycle, or progress-delivery leaks in their own focused issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after regression coverage proves failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the closest merged warning-policy fixes and explicitly scoped this issue as the remaining broader policy decision.
